paper_title: Probing the Blue Axion with Cosmic Optical Background Anisotropies
notes: Blue-axion CDM decaying a->gamma+gamma. Headline measured bound is the solid purple "HST 606 nm" curve in Fig.1 (CDM panel), the recomputed constraint from HST COB anisotropy measurements at 606 nm (Mitchell-Wynne et al. dataset). Extracted as vector strokes from Fig1.pdf (color 0.26,0.22,0.74, solid). Fig1 plots the decay rate Gamma_{a->gg} [s^-1] vs m_a [eV]; converted to g_agamma via Eq.(2) Gamma=g^2 m_a^3/(64pi) in natural units (Gamma[GeV]=Gamma[s^-1]*hbar, hbar=6.582e-25 GeV s). Cross-checked against the e-print file plot_gag.pdf (same figure with y-axis already in g [GeV^-1]); agreement within ~10%. Curve is nearly flat, g~1.5e-11 GeV^-1, min ~1.5e-11 near m_a~9-10 eV, rising to ~2.2e-11 at 25 eV. Fig1 solid line is the conservative bound (C_l not exceeding the upper error bar of any 606 nm data point); Fig8a shows this coincides with the likelihood 95%% C.L. bound to within ~30%%. Limit assumes blue axions are 100%% of CDM (rho_a=rho_CDM, Omega_CDM h^2=0.12); it depends on the cosmological CDM abundance, not a local halo density, so dm_density_assumed is null. HST 438/336 nm curves (dashed) are projections and are not reported.
